source.name: Paleobiology Database (PBDB)
source.license: CC-BY 4.0 (data) — Creative Commons Attribution for compiled occurrence data; PBDB requires attribution to contributors
source.attribution_string: Data from the Paleobiology Database (https://paleobiodb.org) — public, CC-BY 4.0
source.authentication: none — anonymous tier, ~10 req/s sustained, throttled above that

description: PBDB is the canonical open fossil occurrence database, curated by a global community of paleontologists. GEOX uses it as the primary substrate for biostratigraphy (taxon resolution, occurrence records, biozone catalogues, ICS chronostratigraphy). 24h in-process TTL cache keeps traffic well under rate limits.

endpoints.name: taxa/get
endpoints.purpose: Resolve a taxon name → TaxonRecord (pbdb_oid, FAD/LAD, n_occurrences)

endpoints.name: taxa/autocomplete
endpoints.purpose: Fuzzy match for partial taxon names

endpoints.name: taxa/list
endpoints.purpose: List taxa under a parent taxon (e.g. all Coccolithophyceae genera)

endpoints.name: occs/list
endpoints.purpose: List fossil occurrence records with location, age, lithology

endpoints.name: intervals/list
endpoints.purpose: Get biozone / chronostratigraphic intervals. scale=1 (ICS ages), scale=5 (nanno zones), scale=24 (foram zones)

endpoints.name: colls/list
endpoints.purpose: List fossil collection metadata (locality + author + reference)

geo_relevance.malaysia: PBDB coverage of Malaysian fossils is sparse but growing. PMB, Malay Basin, and Sabah have <500 records each. Substrate is more useful for global biostrat calibration than for local occurrence queries.
geo_relevance.sabah_nspw: NSPW (North Sabah Wildlife / North Sabah Basin) has limited PBDB coverage; biostrat work relies on enterprise data + Macrostrat lithostrat
geo_relevance.tier_a_strategy: PBDB is the SUBSTRATE for taxonomic resolution, not a primary local data source. GEOX layer pattern: (1) resolve taxon via PBDB → (2) check Macrostrat for lithostrat context → (3) query JMG MyGEMS for local map layers
